grades.rationale: The YAML preserves rule codes (E501, UP032, unresolved-import) and per-file scope (consumer.py) with all line-producing tools at status=ok, so findings are traceable though the aggregate itself doesn't list lines.
bandit.by_severity is all zero, pip_audit severities all zero, and ruff security=0 — distribution is appropriately uninflated for clean code.
ruff, ty, bandit, radon, complexipy, vulture, pip_audit, detect_secrets all status=ok covering every Python lens; only mypy is not_installed but ty covers typing redundantly.
Every count (ruff total_violations=2, ty total_errors=1) comes from a tool with status=ok, and mypy is explicitly marked not_installed rather than fabricating counts.
Per adaptation note, N/A default; by_rule codes like UP032 and unresolved-import do implicitly pin fix direction.

by_rule cites specific codes (E501, UP032, unresolved-import) for findings, and clean axes show structural evidence (radon total_functions=1, complexipy total_functions=1, bandit total=0) proving tools reached the code.
radon.cc.max=2 with over_threshold_10=0, complexipy.max=2 with over_threshold_15=0, radon.mi.min=61.68 with under_20=0, and halstead.max_volume=27.0 — all measured numbers with thresholds present.
Report is pure structured counts with no editorializing; E501/UP032 are surfaced as tool-detected rule codes rather than style preaching.
